title: Complete Modified Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for one-dimensional quantum Spin Chain
abstract: We prove a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality with a system-size-independent constant for Chen--Kastoryano--Gilyén Gibbs samplers on one-dimensional spin chain at every fixed positive temperature. The result holds for Hamiltonians with bounded finite-range interactions, including noncommuting and spatially nonuniform interactions. It yields trace and diamond mixing times of order $O(\log N+\log(1/ε))$. The proof establishes complete spatial entropy factorization and absorbs quasi-local errors as conditional relative entropy at the original joint state and reference. The static estimate also yields a system-size-independent CMLSI for the single-site Petz heat-bath and regularised heat-bath dynamics.

bite.hook: 1D quantum spin chains can reach thermal equilibrium in logarithmic time, regardless of the chain's overall length.
tldr: Analyzed thermal mixing speeds of quantum Gibbs samplers on one-dimensional spin chains at positive temperatures.
Proved a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality by establishing complete spatial entropy factorization.
Showed trace and diamond mixing times scale as O(log N + log(1/ε)), independent of total system size N.
bite.whyItMatters: Simulating quantum thermal states is a core bottleneck in physics. Knowing that 1D spin chains equilibrate in logarithmic time proves that preparing these thermal states on quantum computers is remarkably efficient.
bite.eli5: Imagine a row of dominoes trying to settle into a relaxed state. Even if the row is millions of dominoes long, the time it takes for thermal chaos to settle down only grows as the logarithm of its length—meaning it happens astonishingly fast.
